b2-13-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking for a Flat
b2-13-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what kind of flat you want in Budapest. You do not have one yet; you want a spacious flat that has a lift.
b2-13-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what kind of flat you are looking for.
cues: Say you are looking for a flat
Say what it should be like
b2-13-01.target: Busco un apartamento que sea amplio y que tenga ascensor.
b2-13-01.english: I'm looking for a flat that is spacious and has a lift.
b2-13-01.canDo: I can describe something I am looking for but have not found, using que + subjunctive.

b2-13-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Is There a Plumber?
b2-13-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you know a plumber for a leak. You do not know anyone who can come today.
b2-13-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you do not know any plumber who can come today.
cues: Say you do not know anyone
Say what that person should be able to do
b2-13-02.target: No conozco a ningún plomero que pueda venir hoy.
b2-13-02.english: I don't know any plumber who can come today.
b2-13-02.canDo: I can say that nobody or nothing fits a description, using nadie, nada or ningún + que + subjunctive.

b2-13-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Right Charger
b2-13-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about your phone charger. You needed one that fitted your phone, and you have found one that works.
b2-13-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you needed and that you found it.
cues: Say what kind of charger you needed
Say that you found one that works
b2-13-03.target: Necesitaba un cargador que sirviera para mi celular y encontré uno que servía.
b2-13-03.english: I needed a charger that would work for my phone and I found one that worked.
b2-13-03.canDo: I can choose between indicative and subjunctive after que by asking whether the thing is real.

b2-13-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Someone to Trust
b2-13-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what kind of person you want to work with in the office. You want someone you can trust.
b2-13-04.prompt: Tell Meg what kind of person you want to work with.
cues: Say you want to work with someone
Say you want to be able to trust that person
b2-13-04.target: Quiero trabajar con alguien en quien pueda confiar.
b2-13-04.english: I want to work with someone I can trust.
b2-13-04.canDo: I can ask for a person or place with a preposition + relative + subjunctive.

b2-13-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Job I Want
b2-13-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what kind of job you would like. You want a job that pays well and has a good schedule.
b2-13-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what kind of job you want.
b2-13-05.target: Quiero un trabajo que pague bien y tenga un buen horario.
b2-13-05.english: I want a job that pays well and has good hours.
b2-13-05.canDo: I can read and write a job ad with que + subjunctive.

b2-13-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Found Yet
b2-13-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you are looking for in a new flat. You want a bright one, and so far you have not found any you like.
b2-13-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what kind of flat you want and that you have not found one.
cues: Say you are looking for a flat and what it should be like
Say you have not found one yet
b2-13-consolidation.target: Busco un apartamento que sea luminoso, pero todavía no he encontrado ninguno que me guste.
b2-13-consolidation.english: I'm looking for a flat that is bright, but I haven't found one I like yet.
b2-13-consolidation.canDo: I can describe what I am looking for with que + subjunctive and tell it from a real thing.
